sections.title: Shelter Animal Medicine
sections.description: This rotation gives a complex overview of the field of shelter medicine and community outreach by partnering via a service-learning model with open and closed admission shelters, HQHV surgical clinics, schools, and outreach organizations like Pets for Life. A typical rotation focuses on authentic hands-on learning including four surgical days, mentored primary case management of medical cases and shelter population rounds, public clinical outreach, herd health management, training and behavioral assessment, and providing veterinary CE for shelter staff. Rounds and tour topics include cruelty investigation and humane law enforcement, behavior, ethics, exotics, and risk analysis. Dentistry, necropsies, consults, special procedures, and outreach to local middle schools can also be included as part of the rotation depending on the week.

sections.title: Shelter Medicine and Community Engagement
sections.description: This rotation gives a complex overview of the field of shelter medicine and community outreach by partnering via a service-learning model with open and limited admission shelters, HQHVSN clinics, schools, and outreach organizations like Pets for Life. A typical rotation focuses on authentic hands-on learning including two-three surgical days, mentored primary case management of medical cases and shelter population rounds, public clinical outreach, herd health management, training and behavioral assessment, outreach to local schools, and providing veterinary CE for shelter staff. Rounds and tour topics include shelter medicine practice, biosecurity, cruelty investigation and humane law enforcement, behavior, ethics, exotics, and risk analysis. Dentistry, necropsies, consults, special procedures, and other opportunities may occasionally be included as part of the rotation depending on the week. Because Penn Vet works with outside organizations, keep in mind the schedule can change as our partners' needs change. This course occurs off-campus in a variety of locations and students must coordinate their own transportation. Two of the three weeks will be in-clinic. One of the three weeks students will have off as determined by the shelter medicine program schedule. Other experiences scheduled by the student, preparation for boards, and/or vacation can be done in the non-clinical week.
